# :236-241), the three-clause exported-hierarchy comparison, the
# one-definition-two-apis rule, and the api overload-set ambiguity check:
#
#   Compiled1.i  Compiled2.a  Compiled3.g  Compiled3.q  Compiled5.bq  Compiled5.y
#
# The three the phase-2 api check mode newly REACHED went the same way in the
# same commits: Compiled3.w.fsi, Compiled5.bp.fss, Compiled5.x.fsi. So did four
# that were listed from before: Compiled0.p, Compiled10.g, Compiled3.r and
# XXXPreparser.c.
#
# ONE OF THE SEVEN IS STILL HERE AND IT IS THE LINE BELOW.
#
#   Compiled1.al  "Item at this location must be an expression, not an
#                  operator", at 15:48, which is the `^` in `f(a)^b`.
#                  RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE OPERATOR GRAMMAR after SPIKE-OPEXPR's
#                  declaration half landed: it still compiles and it computes
#                  the RIGHT ANSWER -- `dbl(3)^2` is 81.
#                  The only spec rule that could refuse it is the
#                  superscripted-postfix rule, lexical-structure.tex:1204-1213,
#                  and that rule EXCLUDES this case by its own wording: `^T` is
#                  a postfix operator "provided that it is not immediately
#                  followed by a word character", and `^b` is not a simple
#                  operator preceded by `^` either.
#                  THE BROAD READING THAT WOULD REFUSE IT COSTS 383 SITES ACROSS
#                  103 FILES, six of them inside the compiling set, and they are
#                  overwhelmingly `^2` and `^3`. So the spec supports US and not
#                  the legacy here.
#                  It stays in THIS file and not in the divergence list because
#                  the gate cannot hold an acceptance there -- `verdict` refuses
#                  to reclassify a case whose detail is "ACCEPTED a program",
#                  deliberately. Defect register DEV-12.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADDED DELIBERATELY, 2026-08-21, WITH ITS REASON -- which is what this file
# asks for; what it forbids is adding a line casually.
#
#   XXXPreparser.c  The legacy refuses it for UNMATCHED DELIMITERS:
#                   `import List.{Cons => CC, opr <| => ||}` leaves `<|` open
#                   as far as its preparser is concerned, and it reports three
#                   errors none of which we implement.
#                   IT WAS ONLY EVER REFUSED HERE BY ACCIDENT. Until the
#                   resolver read the import list, this file merged the WHOLE
#                   of `List` and died on `unknown type LexicographicOrder` --
#                   a name it never mentions. Fixing the resolver removed the
#                   accident and revealed we accept the program. That is an
#                   exposure, not a regression: the refusal was never ours.
#                   OUR PARSE IS STRUCTURALLY CORRECT, checked rather than
#                   assumed: the import records `Cons => CC` and `<| => ||`,
#                   two aliased names, which is what the source says. The gap
#                   is that 1.0 wants its PREPARSER to refuse the program
#                   before a parse is attempted at all -- the file is named
#                   XXXPreparser on purpose. So we are MORE PERMISSIVE, not
#                   more correct.
#                   Re-opens with delimiter matching in the preparser, which is
#                   real work and is nobody's item yet.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ProjectFortress/parser_tests/XXXPreparser.c.fss

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADDED AT THE OBJECT/ANY MERGE, 2026-08-22, WITH ITS REASON.
#
#   Compiled5.j  The legacy refuses it for "Invalid overloading of f":
#                `f(a:A)` and `f(b:B)` where `trait C extends {A,B}`.
#                IT WAS NOT REFUSED HERE BY THAT RULE. Until `Object` was a
#                type it died on `f(o:Object)` -- `unknown type Object` -- so
#                the refusal was an accident of the missing seed, exactly as
#                XXXPreparser.c was an accident of the import resolver.
#                OUR ACCEPTANCE IS THE RECORDED CLOSED-WORLD DEVIATION and not
#                a new one: dispatch here enumerates every tuple of CONCRETE
#                types reaching the set, and `A comprises {At,C}` while
#                `B comprises {Bt,C}`, so the only value reaching both arms is
#                a `C` and `f(c:C)` is its unique most-specific winner. 1.0
#                asks the question open-world, where some later type could
#                extend A and B without extending C.
#                CHECKED BY RUNNING IT rather than by exit 0: it prints
#                `A`, `B`, `C`, which is what the three calls mean.
#                Re-opens if exclusion ever becomes open-world; it will not.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/Compiled5.j.fss

# NAMED HERE AS A COMMENT AND NOT AS A LINE, 2026-08-22, AND THAT IS FORCED.
#
# The ruling was "add XXXOprMethod.fss to this list with a written reason".
# A LINE WOULD NOT SURVIVE. `rewrite_list` above regenerates this file from
# `accepted`, which is built from cases whose `.test` records
# `compile_err_equals`/`compile_err_contains`. XXXOprMethod.fss has NO `.test`
# at all, so it can never be in `wanted`, and the first `--refresh-lists` after
# the line went in would DROP it -- silently, because dropping is what that
# function is for. A comment is never dropped, so this is the durable form of
# the same record. The reason, which is the point of the ruling:
#
#   ProjectFortress/parser_tests/XXXOprMethod.fss
#                We ACCEPT it and the XXX convention says the legacy REFUSED
#                it. It declares `opr IN(c:Char): Boolean` and `opr [i:ZZ32]`
#                as object members. It was refused HERE until 2026-08-22 for a
#                reason that had nothing to do with operator methods: `Char`
#                was not a type. SPIKE-OPEXPR records operator declarations and
#                NOTHING READS THEM, so what it compiles to is a program whose
#                two declarations do nothing and whose `run()` returns ().
#                WE DO NOT KNOW 1.0's SPECIFIC GROUND FOR REFUSING IT AND ARE
#                NOT INVENTING ONE. A blind refusal rule keyed on "an object
#                declares an `opr` member" would be a guess, and it would also
#                refuse the subscript-operator work that M3c's dispatch will
#                need. So the acceptance is tolerated and written down instead.
#                THE RATCHET THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS IT is apply-gate's slack, not
#                this file: tools/apply-gate.sh:261-269 counts it, with
#                XXXequalityTesting.fss, into the slack of 40 behind
#                OBJECT_FLOOR=321. Re-opens the day operator declarations are
#                READ, which is SPIKE-OPEXPR's own milestone.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
